zh: 初，太后弟秉，以功封都鄉侯，黃初七年進封開陽侯，邑千二百戶，爲昭烈將軍。
literal: At first, the empress dowager's younger brother Bing, for merit, was enfeoffed as Marquis of the Capital Village; in the seventh year of Huangchu he was advanced to Marquis of Kaiyang with a fief of one thousand two hundred households and made General Who Displays Fierce Valor.
idiomatic: At first the empress dowager's younger brother Bing was enfeoffed as Marquis of the Capital Village for his service. In Huangchu 7 he was promoted to Marquis of Kaiyang with a fief of twelve hundred households and made General Who Displays Fierce Valor.

zh: 《魏略》曰：初，卞后弟秉，當建安時得爲別部司馬，后常對太祖怨言，太祖荅言：「但得與我作婦弟，不爲多邪？」
literal: The Wei Summary states: At first, Empress Bian's younger brother Bing, during the Jian'an era, was able to become a Separate Commandment Major; the empress often voiced grievances to the Grand Progenitor about him, and the Grand Progenitor replied, saying, "Is it not already much that he gets to be my brother-in-law?"
idiomatic: The Wei Summary says that during Jian'an, Empress Bian's brother Bing became a separate commandment major. The empress often complained about him to the Grand Progenitor, who answered, "Is it not already much that he gets to be my brother-in-law?"

zh: 后又欲太祖給其錢帛，太祖又曰：「但汝盜與，不爲足邪？」
literal: Later the empress also wanted the Grand Progenitor to supply him with money and silks; the Grand Progenitor again said, "Is it not enough that you secretly give to him?"
idiomatic: Later she also wanted the Grand Progenitor to supply him with money and silks. He replied again, "Is it not enough that you secretly give to him?"

zh: 故訖太祖世，秉官不移，財亦不益。
literal: Therefore throughout the Grand Progenitor's lifetime Bing's office did not change and his wealth was not increased.
idiomatic: So throughout the Grand Progenitor's lifetime Bing's office never changed and his wealth was never increased.

zh: 秉薨，子蘭嗣。
literal: When Bing died, his son Lan succeeded.
idiomatic: When Bing died, his son Lan succeeded.

zh: 少有才學，《魏略》曰：蘭獻賦贊述太子德美，太子報曰：「賦者，言事類之所附也，頌者，美盛德之形容也，故作者不虛其辭，受者必當其實。
literal: He had talent and learning from youth. The Wei Summary states: Lan presented fu and praise describing the heir apparent's virtuous beauty; the heir apparent replied, saying, "The fu states the categories to which affairs attach; the song praises the appearance of flourishing virtue. Therefore the author must not empty his words, and the recipient must match the reality.
idiomatic: He showed talent and learning from youth. The Wei Summary says Lan presented fu and praise describing the heir apparent's virtues. The heir apparent replied, "The fu states the categories to which affairs attach; the song praises the form of flourishing virtue. The author must not empty his words, and the recipient must match the reality.

zh: 蘭此賦，豈吾實哉？
literal: Is this fu of Lan truly my reality?
idiomatic: Is this fu of Lan truly my reality?

zh: 昔吾丘壽王一陳寶鼎，何武等徒以歌頌，猶受金帛之賜，蘭事雖不諒，義足嘉也。
literal: In former times when Liu Qiu, King Shou of Wu, once presented the precious tripod, He Wu and the rest merely sang in praise yet still received gifts of gold and silks. Lan's matter, though not to be credited, is worthy enough to commend.
idiomatic: When Liu Qiu, King Shou of Wu, once presented the precious tripod, He Wu and others merely sang in praise yet still received gold and silks. Lan's matter, though not to be credited, is still worthy of commendation.

zh: 今賜牛一頭。」
literal: Now I grant one ox."
idiomatic: Now I grant one ox."

zh: 由是遂見親敬。
literal: From this he came to be treated with intimacy and respect.
idiomatic: From this he came to be treated with intimacy and respect.

zh: 爲奉車都尉、游擊將軍，加散騎常侍。
literal: He served as Commandant of the Imperial Carriage and General Who Attacks Independently, with the additional post of Regular Attendant.
idiomatic: He served as commandant of the imperial carriage and general who attacks independently, with the additional post of regular attendant.

zh: 蘭薨，子暉嗣。
literal: When Lan died, his son Hui succeeded.
idiomatic: When Lan died, his son Hui succeeded.

zh: 《魏略》曰：明帝時，蘭見外有二難，而帝留意於宮室，常因侍從，數切諫。
literal: The Wei Summary states: During Ming-di's reign Lan saw that externally there were two difficulties while the emperor focused on palace construction; he often took occasion while attending in close service to remonstrate sharply and repeatedly.
idiomatic: The Wei Summary says that during Ming-di's reign Lan saw two external crises while the emperor focused on palace construction. He often remonstrated sharply while attending in close service.

zh: 帝雖不能從，猶納其誠欵。
literal: Although the emperor could not follow his advice, he still accepted his sincere devotion.
idiomatic: Although the emperor could not follow his advice, he still accepted his sincere devotion.

zh: 後蘭苦酒消渴，時帝信巫女用水方，使人持水賜蘭，蘭不肯飲。
literal: Later Lan suffered from wine-induced thirst; at the time the emperor trusted a shamaness's water prescription and sent someone bearing water to grant to Lan, but Lan refused to drink.
idiomatic: Later Lan suffered from wine-induced thirst. The emperor trusted a shamaness's water prescription and sent water for him, but Lan refused to drink.

zh: 詔問其意？
literal: An edict asked his meaning?
idiomatic: An edict asked why.

zh: 蘭言治病自當以方藥，何信於此？
literal: Lan said that treating illness should naturally rely on prescriptions and medicines—why trust in this?
idiomatic: Lan said illness should be treated with prescriptions and medicines—why trust in this?

zh: 帝爲變色，而蘭終不服。
literal: The emperor changed countenance, yet Lan to the end did not submit.
idiomatic: The emperor changed countenance, yet Lan to the end would not submit.

zh: 後渴稍甚，以至於亡。
literal: Later his thirst grew somewhat worse, until it led to his death.
idiomatic: Later his thirst grew worse until he died.

zh: 故時人見蘭好直言，謂帝靣折之而蘭自殺，其實不然。
literal: Therefore people of the time, seeing Lan's love of blunt speech, said the emperor had shamed him to his face and Lan killed himself—but in fact it was not so.
idiomatic: People of the time, seeing Lan's love of blunt speech, said the emperor had shamed him to his face and Lan killed himself—but in fact it was not so.

zh: 又分秉爵，封蘭弟琳爲列侯，官至步兵校尉。
literal: Bing's noble rank was also divided, and Lan's younger brother Lin was enfeoffed as a full marquis, reaching the office of Colonel of the Footsoldiers.
idiomatic: Bing's noble rank was also divided, and Lan's younger brother Lin was enfeoffed as a full marquis and reached the office of colonel of the footsoldiers.

zh: 蘭子隆女爲高貴鄉公皇后，隆以后父爲光祿大夫，位特進，封睢陽鄉侯，妻王爲顯陽鄉君。
literal: Lan's son Long had a daughter who became empress to the Duke of Gaoguixiang; Long, as the empress's father, was made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the position of Special Advance, enfeoffed as Marquis of Suiyang Village, and his wife Wang was made Lady of Xianyang Village.
idiomatic: Lan's son Long had a daughter who became empress to the Duke of Gaoguixiang. Long, as the empress's father, was made grand master for splendid happiness with the rank of special advance, enfeoffed as Marquis of Suiyang village, and his wife Wang was made lady of Xianyang village.

zh: 追封隆前妻劉爲順陽鄉君，后親母故也。
literal: Long's former wife Liu was posthumously enfeoffed as Lady of Shunyang Village, because she was the empress's birth mother.
idiomatic: Long's former wife Liu was posthumously enfeoffed as lady of Shunyang village, because she was the empress's birth mother.

zh: 琳女又爲陳留王皇后，時琳已沒，封琳妻劉爲廣陽鄉君。
literal: Lin's daughter also became empress to the Prince of Chenliu; Lin was already dead, so Lin's wife Liu was enfeoffed as Lady of Guangyang Village.
idiomatic: Lin's daughter also became empress to the Prince of Chenliu. Lin was already dead, so his wife Liu was enfeoffed as lady of Guangyang village.

zh: 文昭甄皇后，中山無極人，明帝母，漢太保甄邯後也，世吏二千石。
literal: Empress Wen-Zhao, née Zhen, was a native of Wuji in Zhongshan, mother of Ming-di, a descendant of Han's Grand Tutor Zhen Han; for generations her family held offices of two thousand shi.
idiomatic: Empress Wen-Zhao of the Zhen clan came from Wuji in Zhongshan. She was Ming-di's mother and a descendant of Han's grand tutor Zhen Han; for generations her family held offices of two thousand shi.

zh: 父逸，上蔡令。
literal: Her father Yi was Magistrate of Shangcai.
idiomatic: Her father Yi was magistrate of Shangcai.

zh: 后三歲失父。
literal: The empress lost her father at age three.
idiomatic: The empress lost her father at age three.

zh: 《魏書》曰：逸娶常山張氏，生三男五女：長男豫，早終；
literal: The Book of Wei states: Yi married a woman of the Zhang clan of Changshan and had three sons and five daughters: the eldest son Yu died early;
idiomatic: The Book of Wei says Yi married a woman of the Zhang clan of Changshan and had three sons and five daughters: the eldest son Yu died early;

zh: 次儼，舉孝廉，大將軍掾、曲梁長；
literal: the second, Yan, was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt, served as aide to the Grand General, and was Magistrate of Quliang;
idiomatic: the second, Yan, was recommended as filial and incorrupt, served as aide to the grand general, and was magistrate of Quliang;

zh: 次堯，舉孝廉；
literal: the third, Yao, was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt;
idiomatic: the third, Yao, was recommended as filial and incorrupt;

zh: 長女姜，次脫，次道，次榮，次即后。
literal: the eldest daughter Jiang, then Tuo, then Dao, then Rong, and last was the empress.
idiomatic: the eldest daughter Jiang, then Tuo, then Dao, then Rong, and last the empress.

zh: 后以漢光和五年十二月丁酉生。
literal: The empress was born on the dingyou day of the twelfth month of the fifth year of Guanghe of Han.
idiomatic: The empress was born on dingyou in the twelfth month of Han Guanghe 5.

zh: 每寢寐，家中彷彿見如有人持玉衣覆其上者，常共怪之。
literal: Whenever she slept, the household seemed to see as if someone held a jade garment covering her; they constantly marveled at it together.
idiomatic: Whenever she slept, the household seemed to see someone holding a jade garment over her, and they all marveled at it.

zh: 逸薨，加號慕，內外益奇之。
literal: When Yi died, her grief was called deep and yearning; inside and outside the family all the more found her extraordinary.
idiomatic: When Yi died, her deep mourning made everyone inside and outside the family find her all the more extraordinary.

zh: 後相者劉良相后及諸子，良指后曰：「此女貴乃不可言。」
literal: Later the physiognomist Liu Liang read the empress and all the children; Liang pointed to the empress and said, "This girl's nobility is beyond words."
idiomatic: Later the physiognomist Liu Liang read the empress and all the children. Pointing to her he said, "This girl's nobility is beyond words."

zh: 后自少至長，不好戲弄。
literal: From youth to adulthood the empress did not care for playful amusement.
idiomatic: From youth to adulthood the empress cared nothing for playful amusement.

zh: 年八歲，外有立騎馬戲者，家人諸姊皆上閣觀之，后獨不行。
literal: At age eight, outside there were performers standing on horseback; all the sisters in the family went up to the gallery to watch, but the empress alone would not go.
idiomatic: At age eight, when mounted performers put on a show outside, all her sisters went up to the gallery to watch, but the empress alone would not go.

zh: 諸姊怪問之，后答言：「此豈女人之所觀邪？」
literal: Her sisters wondered and asked her; the empress answered, saying, "Is this something a woman should watch?"
idiomatic: Her sisters wondered and asked her. She answered, "Is this something a woman should watch?"

zh: 年九歲，喜書，視字輒識，數用諸兄筆硯，兄謂后言：「汝當習女工。
literal: At age nine she loved books; seeing characters she immediately knew them, and often used her elder brothers' brush and inkstone. An elder brother said to the empress, "You should practice women's work.
idiomatic: At age nine she loved books; seeing characters she immediately knew them, and often used her elder brothers' brush and inkstone. An elder brother told her, "You should practice women's work.

zh: 用書為學，當作女博士邪？」
literal: To take books as learning—are you to become a female scholar?"
idiomatic: To take books as learning—are you to become a female scholar?"

zh: 后答言：「聞古者賢女，未有不學前世成敗，以為己誡。
literal: The empress answered, saying, "I have heard that in antiquity worthy women all studied the successes and failures of former ages and took them as warnings for themselves.
idiomatic: She answered, "I have heard that in antiquity worthy women all studied the successes and failures of former ages and took them as warnings for themselves.

zh: 不知書，何由見之？」
literal: Without knowing books, how could one see them?"
idiomatic: Without knowing books, how could one see them?"

zh: 後天下兵亂，加以饑饉，百姓皆賣金銀珠玉寶物，時后家大有儲谷，頗以買之。
literal: Later the realm fell into military disorder, and famine was added; common people all sold gold, silver, pearls, jade, and precious goods. At the time the empress's family had great stores of grain and bought such things in considerable quantity.
idiomatic: Later the realm fell into war and famine, and common people sold gold, silver, pearls, jade, and precious goods. The empress's family had great stores of grain and bought such things in considerable quantity.

zh: 后年十餘歲，白母曰：「今世亂而多買寶物，匹夫無罪，懷璧為罪。
literal: When the empress was just over ten she told her mother, saying, "In this age of disorder, to buy many precious goods—an ordinary man without guilt becomes guilty for holding a jade disc.
idiomatic: When she was just over ten she told her mother, "In this age of disorder, to buy many precious goods—an ordinary man without guilt becomes guilty for holding a jade disc.

zh: 又左右皆飢乏，不如以穀振給親族鄰里，廣為恩惠也。」
literal: Moreover, those around us are all hungry and in want—it would be better to use grain to relieve and supply kin and neighbors and spread kindness broadly."
idiomatic: Moreover, those around us are all hungry and in want. It would be better to use grain to relieve kin and neighbors and spread kindness broadly."

zh: 舉家稱善，即從后言。
literal: The whole family praised this as good and immediately followed the empress's words.
idiomatic: The whole family praised this as good and immediately followed her advice.

zh: 《魏略》曰：后年十四，喪中兄儼，悲哀過制，事寡嫂謙敬，事處其勞，拊養儼子，慈愛甚篤。
literal: The Wei Summary states: At age fourteen the empress mourned her elder brother Yan; her grief exceeded the prescribed measure. She served her widowed sister-in-law with modest reverence, took on the labor in affairs, and nurtured Yan's son with deep loving care.
idiomatic: The Wei Summary says that at age fourteen she mourned her elder brother Yan with grief beyond the prescribed measure. She served her widowed sister-in-law with modest reverence, took on the labor herself, and nurtured Yan's son with deep loving care.

zh: 后母性嚴，待諸婦有常，后數諫母：「兄不幸早終，嫂年少守節，顧留一子，以大義言之，待之當如婦，愛之宜如女。」
literal: The empress's mother was strict by nature and treated the various daughters-in-law with fixed rules. The empress repeatedly admonished her mother: "Elder brother unhappily died early; sister-in-law is young and keeps chastity, yet she has left one son. Speaking by great principle, she should be treated as a daughter-in-law and loved as a daughter."
idiomatic: The empress's mother was strict by nature and treated the daughters-in-law by fixed rules. The empress repeatedly admonished her: "Elder brother died early; sister-in-law is young and keeps chastity, yet she has left one son. By great principle she should be treated as a daughter-in-law and loved as a daughter."

zh: 母感后言流涕，便令后與嫂共止，寢息坐起常相隨，恩愛益密。
literal: The mother was moved by the empress's words to weeping and immediately had the empress and sister-in-law lodge together; in sleeping, rising, sitting, and moving they constantly kept each other company, and their affection grew ever closer.
idiomatic: The mother was moved to tears and had the empress lodge with her sister-in-law. In sleeping, rising, sitting, and moving they constantly kept each other company, and their affection grew ever closer.

zh: 建安中，袁紹為中子熙納之。
literal: During Jian'an, Yuan Shao had his middle son Xi take her in marriage.
idiomatic: During Jian'an, Yuan Shao had his middle son Xi take her in marriage.

zh: 熙出為幽州，后留養姑。
literal: Xi went out to You Province, and the empress remained to nurture her mother-in-law.
idiomatic: Xi went out to You Province, and she remained to care for her mother-in-law.

zh: 及冀州平，文帝納后於鄴，有寵，生明帝及東鄉公主。
literal: When Ji Province was pacified, Wen-di took the empress in marriage at Ye; she had favor and bore Ming-di and the Princess of Dongxiang.
idiomatic: When Ji Province was pacified, Wen-di took her in marriage at Ye. She won favor and bore Ming-di and the Princess of Dongxiang.

zh: 《魏略》曰：熙出在幽州，后留侍姑。
literal: The Wei Summary states: Xi went out to You Province, and the empress remained to attend her mother-in-law.
idiomatic: The Wei Summary says Xi went out to You Province and she remained to attend her mother-in-law.

zh: 及鄴城破，紹妻及后共坐皇堂上。
literal: When Ye city fell, Yuan Shao's wife and the empress sat together in the main hall.
idiomatic: When Ye fell, Yuan Shao's wife and the empress sat together in the main hall.

zh: 文帝入紹舍，見紹妻及后，后怖，以頭伏姑膝上，紹妻兩手自搏。
literal: Wen-di entered Yuan Shao's residence and saw Yuan Shao's wife and the empress; the empress was afraid and laid her head on her mother-in-law's knee, while Yuan Shao's wife beat her own hands together.
idiomatic: Wen-di entered Yuan Shao's residence and saw Yuan Shao's wife and the empress. She was afraid and laid her head on her mother-in-law's knee, while Yuan Shao's wife beat her own hands together.

zh: 文帝謂曰：「劉夫人云何如此？
literal: Wen-di said, "Lady Liu, why are you like this?
idiomatic: Wen-di said, "Lady Liu, why are you like this?

zh: 令新婦舉頭！」
literal: Have the new bride lift her head!"
idiomatic: Have the new bride lift her head!"

zh: 姑乃捧后令仰，文帝就視，見其顏色非凡，稱嘆之。
literal: The mother-in-law then lifted the empress and made her raise her face; Wen-di drew near to look and saw her countenance was extraordinary, and praised her in admiration.
idiomatic: The mother-in-law lifted her and made her raise her face. Wen-di drew near to look, saw her extraordinary beauty, and praised her in admiration.

zh: 太祖聞其意，遂為迎取。
literal: The Grand Progenitor heard of his intent and thereupon had her welcomed and taken.
idiomatic: The Grand Progenitor heard of his intent and had her welcomed and taken.

zh: 《世語》曰：太祖下鄴，文帝先入袁尚府，有婦人被髮垢面，垂涕立紹妻劉後，文帝問之，劉答「是熙妻」，顧攬髮髻，以巾拭面，姿貌絕倫。
literal: Accounts of the Age states: When the Grand Progenitor descended on Ye, Wen-di first entered Yuan Shang's mansion. A woman with hair loose and face filthy stood weeping behind Yuan Shao's wife Liu. Wen-di asked about her; Liu answered, "She is Xi's wife." She turned, gathered her hair into a bun, wiped her face with a kerchief, and her bearing and beauty were unmatched.
idiomatic: Accounts of the Age says that when the Grand Progenitor descended on Ye, Wen-di first entered Yuan Shang's mansion. A woman with hair loose and face filthy stood weeping behind Yuan Shao's wife Liu. Wen-di asked about her; Liu answered, "She is Xi's wife." She turned, gathered her hair into a bun, wiped her face with a kerchief, and her bearing and beauty were unmatched.

zh: 既過，劉謂后「不憂死矣」！
literal: After he had passed, Liu said to the empress, "You need not fear death now!"
idiomatic: After he had passed, Liu told her, "You need not fear death now!"

zh: 遂見納，有寵。
literal: She was then taken in marriage and had favor.
idiomatic: She was then taken in marriage and won favor.

zh: 《魏書》曰：后寵愈隆而彌自挹損，後宮有寵者勸勉之，其無寵者慰誨之，每因閒宴，常勸帝，言「昔黃帝子孫蕃育，蓋由妾媵眾多，乃獲斯祚耳。
literal: The Book of Wei states: As the empress's favor grew ever greater she all the more restrained herself. To favored women of the inner palace she offered encouragement; to those without favor she gave comfort and instruction. At every idle banquet she often urged the emperor, saying, "In former times the Yellow Emperor's descendants multiplied and flourished—likely because concubines and secondary wives were many, and thereby this blessing was obtained.
idiomatic: The Book of Wei says that as her favor grew ever greater she all the more restrained herself. To favored women of the inner palace she offered encouragement; to those without favor she gave comfort and instruction. At every idle banquet she often urged the emperor, saying, "In former times the Yellow Emperor's descendants multiplied and flourished—likely because concubines and secondary wives were many, and thereby this blessing was obtained.

zh: 所原廣求淑媛，以豐繼嗣。」
literal: What I desire is broadly to seek worthy maidens to enrich the succession."
idiomatic: What I desire is broadly to seek worthy maidens to enrich the succession."

zh: 帝心嘉焉。
literal: The emperor's heart approved this.
idiomatic: The emperor's heart approved this.

zh: 其後帝欲遣任氏，后請於帝曰：「任既鄉黨名族，德、色，妾等不及也，如何遣之？」
literal: Afterward the emperor wished to send away Lady Ren. The empress pleaded with the emperor, saying, "Ren is a famous clan of our native district; in virtue and beauty your handmaids do not match her—how can you send her away?"
idiomatic: Afterward the emperor wished to send away Lady Ren. The empress pleaded with him, saying, "Ren is a famous clan of our native district; in virtue and beauty we do not match her—how can you send her away?"

zh: 帝曰：「任性狷急不婉順，前後忿吾非一，是以遣之耳。」
literal: The emperor said, "Ren's nature is narrow and urgent, not gentle and compliant; before and after she has been angry with me more than once—therefore I send her away."
idiomatic: The emperor said, "Ren's nature is narrow and urgent, not gentle and compliant; before and after she has been angry with me more than once—therefore I send her away."

zh: 后流涕固請曰：「妾受敬遇之恩，眾人所知，必謂任之出，是妾之由。
literal: The empress wept and firmly pleaded, saying, "Your handmaid has received the grace of respectful treatment—this all know. They will surely say Ren's dismissal is because of your handmaid.
idiomatic: The empress wept and firmly pleaded, saying, "Your handmaid has received the grace of respectful treatment—this all know. They will surely say Ren's dismissal is because of me.

zh: 上懼有見私之譏，下受專寵之罪，原重留意！」
literal: Above I fear the reproach of showing partiality; below I would bear the guilt of monopolizing favor—I beg you to reconsider carefully!"
idiomatic: Above I fear the reproach of showing partiality; below I would bear the guilt of monopolizing favor—I beg you to reconsider carefully!"

zh: 帝不聽，遂出之。
literal: The emperor did not listen and thereupon sent her out.
idiomatic: The emperor did not listen and sent her out.

zh: 十六年七月，太祖徵關中，武宣皇后從，留孟津，帝居守鄴。
literal: In the seventh month of the sixteenth year the Grand Progenitor campaigned against Guanzhong; Empress Dowager Wu-Xuan followed, remaining at Mengjin, while the emperor stayed to guard Ye.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of year sixteen the Grand Progenitor campaigned against Guanzhong. Empress Dowager Wu-Xuan followed and remained at Mengjin, while Wen-di stayed to guard Ye.

zh: 時武宣皇后體小不安，后不得定省，憂怖，晝夜泣涕；
literal: At the time Empress Dowager Wu-Xuan's body was slightly unwell; the empress could not attend to inquire after her and was anxious and fearful, weeping day and night;
idiomatic: At the time Empress Dowager Wu-Xuan was slightly unwell. The empress could not attend to inquire after her and was anxious and fearful, weeping day and night;

zh: 左右驟以差問告，后猶不信，曰：「夫人在家，故疾每動，輒歷時，今疾便差，何速也？
literal: attendants suddenly reported that she had improved; the empress still did not believe and said, "When the lady was at home, whenever her old illness stirred it always lasted some time. Now the illness has suddenly improved—how can it be so quick?
idiomatic: attendants suddenly reported that she had improved. The empress still did not believe and said, "When the lady was at home, whenever her old illness stirred it always lasted some time. Now the illness has suddenly improved—how can it be so quick?

zh: 此欲慰我意耳！」
literal: This is only to comfort my feelings!"
idiomatic: This is only to comfort my feelings!"

zh: 憂愈甚。
literal: Her worry grew all the greater.
idiomatic: Her worry grew all the greater.

zh: 后得武宣皇后還書，說疾已平復，后乃懽悅。
literal: When the empress received Empress Dowager Wu-Xuan's reply saying the illness had already fully recovered, she then rejoiced.
idiomatic: When she received Empress Dowager Wu-Xuan's reply saying the illness had fully recovered, she rejoiced.

zh: 十七年正月，大軍還鄴，后朝武宣皇后，望幄座悲喜，感動左右。
literal: In the first month of the seventeenth year the great army returned to Ye; the empress attended upon Empress Dowager Wu-Xuan, and gazing at the curtained seat felt both grief and joy, moving those around her.
idiomatic: In the first month of year seventeen the great army returned to Ye. The empress attended upon Empress Dowager Wu-Xuan, and gazing at the curtained seat felt both grief and joy, moving those around her.

zh: 武宣皇后見后如此，亦泣，且謂之曰：「新婦謂吾前病如昔時困邪？
literal: Empress Dowager Wu-Xuan, seeing the empress like this, also wept and said to her, "Does the new bride think my former illness was like the distress of former times?
idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wu-Xuan, seeing her like this, also wept and said, "Does the new bride think my former illness was like the distress of former times?

zh: 吾時小小耳，十餘日即差，不當視我顏色乎！」
literal: At the time it was only slight; in little more than ten days it was cured—you should not have looked at my complexion so!"
idiomatic: At the time it was only slight; in little more than ten days it was cured—you should not have looked at my complexion so!"

zh: 嗟歎曰：「此真孝婦也。」
literal: She sighed in admiration and said, "This is truly a filial daughter-in-law."
idiomatic: She sighed in admiration and said, "This is truly a filial daughter-in-law."

zh: 二十一年，太祖東征，武宣皇后、文帝及明帝、東鄉公主皆從，時后以病留鄴。
literal: In the twenty-first year the Grand Progenitor campaigned east; Empress Dowager Wu-Xuan, Wen-di, Ming-di, and the Princess of Dongxiang all followed, while at the time the empress remained at Ye because of illness.
idiomatic: In year twenty-one the Grand Progenitor campaigned east. Empress Dowager Wu-Xuan, Wen-di, Ming-di, and the Princess of Dongxiang all followed, while the empress remained at Ye because of illness.

zh: 二十二年九月，大軍還，武宣皇后左右侍御見后顏色豐盈，怪問之曰：「后與二子別久，下流之情，不可為念，而后顏色更盛，何也？」
literal: In the ninth month of the twenty-second year the great army returned; attendants around Empress Dowager Wu-Xuan saw the empress's complexion full and flourishing, wondered, and asked, saying, "The empress has been apart from her two sons for long; the feelings of parting should not be forgotten, yet her complexion is even more radiant—why?"
idiomatic: In the ninth month of year twenty-two the great army returned. Attendants around Empress Dowager Wu-Xuan saw the empress's complexion full and flourishing, wondered, and asked, "The empress has been apart from her two sons for long; the feelings of parting should not be forgotten, yet her complexion is even more radiant—why?"

zh: 后笑答之曰：「
literal: The empress laughed and answered, saying, "
idiomatic: The empress laughed and answered, "

literal: (tabooed)
idiomatic: (tabooed)

zh: 等自隨夫人，我當何憂！」
literal: and the rest follow the lady by themselves—what should I worry about!"
idiomatic: and the rest follow the lady by themselves—what should I worry about!"

zh: 后之賢明以禮自持如此。
literal: The empress's wisdom and clarity, holding herself by ritual, were like this.
idiomatic: Such was the empress's wisdom and restraint in holding herself by ritual.

zh: 延康元年220年正月，文帝即王位，六月，南征，后留鄴。
literal: In the first month of the first year of Yankang (220 CE) Wen-di took the royal title; in the sixth month he campaigned south, and the empress remained at Ye.
idiomatic: In the first month of Yankang 1 (220 CE) Wen-di took the royal title. In the sixth month he campaigned south, and the empress remained at Ye.

zh: 黃初元年十月，帝踐阼。
literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Huangchu the emperor ascended the throne.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of Huangchu 1 the emperor ascended the throne.

zh: 踐阼之後，山陽公奉二女以嬪於魏，郭后、李、陰貴人並愛幸，后愈失意，有怨言。
literal: After ascending the throne, the Duke of Shanyang presented two daughters to become consorts of Wei; Empress Guo and the Honored Ladies Li and Yin were all favored and cherished; the empress grew ever more disappointed and had resentful words.
idiomatic: After ascending the throne, the Duke of Shanyang presented two daughters to become consorts of Wei. Empress Guo and the Honored Ladies Li and Yin were all favored, and the empress grew ever more disappointed and spoke resentfully.

zh: 帝大怒，二年六月，遣使賜死，葬於鄴。
literal: The emperor was greatly angered; in the sixth month of the second year he sent an envoy to grant death, and she was buried at Ye.
idiomatic: The emperor was greatly angered. In the sixth month of year two he sent an envoy to grant death, and she was buried at Ye.

zh: 《魏書》曰：有司奏建長秋宮，帝璽書迎后，詣行在所，后上表曰：「妾聞先代之興，所以饗國久長，垂祚後嗣，無不由后妃焉。
literal: The Book of Wei states: The responsible officials memorialized to establish the Palace of Everlasting Autumn; the emperor sent an imperial patent to welcome the empress to the traveling residence. The empress submitted a memorial, saying, "Your handmaid has heard that the rise of former ages, whereby states were nourished long and blessings were handed down to later heirs, was never without empresses and consorts.
idiomatic: The Book of Wei says officials memorialized to establish the Palace of Everlasting Autumn, and the emperor sent an imperial patent to welcome the empress to the traveling residence. She submitted a memorial, saying, "Your handmaid has heard that the rise of former ages, whereby states were nourished long and blessings were handed down to later heirs, was never without empresses and consorts.

zh: 故必審選其人，以興內教。
literal: Therefore one must carefully select the person to raise inner instruction.
idiomatic: Therefore one must carefully select the person to raise inner instruction.

zh: 令踐阼之初，誠宜登進賢淑，統理六宮。
literal: Now at the beginning of ascending the throne it is truly fitting to advance the worthy and virtuous to govern the six palaces.
idiomatic: Now at the beginning of ascending the throne it is truly fitting to advance the worthy and virtuous to govern the six palaces.

zh: 妾自省愚陋，不任粢盛之事，加以寢疾，敢守微志。」
literal: Your handmaid examines herself as foolish and base, unfit for the charge of sacrificial grain, and moreover afflicted with lingering illness—I dare hold to my modest wish."
idiomatic: Your handmaid examines herself as foolish and base, unfit for the charge of sacrificial grain, and moreover afflicted with lingering illness—I dare hold to my modest wish."

zh: 璽書三至而后三讓，言甚懇切。
literal: Imperial patents came three times and the empress yielded three times; her words were very earnest and sincere.
idiomatic: Imperial patents came three times and she yielded three times; her words were very earnest and sincere.

zh: 時盛暑，帝欲須秋涼乃更迎后。
literal: It was then the height of summer; the emperor wished to wait until autumn's cool before welcoming the empress again.
idiomatic: It was then the height of summer; the emperor wished to wait until autumn's cool before welcoming her again.

zh: 會后疾遂篤，夏六月丁卯，崩於鄴。
literal: But the empress's illness then grew grave; on dingmao in the sixth month of summer she died at Ye.
idiomatic: But her illness then grew grave. On dingmao in the sixth month of summer she died at Ye.

zh: 帝哀痛咨嗟，策贈皇后璽綬。
literal: The emperor mourned in grief and lamentation and by patent granted the empress's seal and sash.
idiomatic: The emperor mourned in grief and lamentation and by patent granted the empress's seal and sash.

zh: 臣松之以為春秋之義，內大惡諱，小惡不書。
literal: Your servant Songzhi considers that by the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals, great evils within are tabooed and not written, while small evils are not recorded.
idiomatic: Pei Songzhi considers that by the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals, great evils within are tabooed and not written, while small evils are not recorded.

zh: 文帝之不立甄氏，及加殺害，事有明審。
literal: Wen-di's not establishing the Zhen clan, and moreover adding execution—the matter is clearly established.
idiomatic: Wen-di's not establishing Lady Zhen, and moreover putting her to death—the matter is clearly established.

zh: 魏史若以為大惡邪，則宜隱而不言，若謂為小惡邪，則不應假為之辭，而崇飾虛文乃至於是，異乎所聞於舊史。
literal: If the Wei historians considered it a great evil, then they should have concealed it and not spoken; if they called it a small evil, then they should not have fabricated words for it and exalted and adorned empty prose to this extent—this differs from what one hears in the old histories.
idiomatic: If the Wei historians considered it a great evil, they should have concealed it and not spoken; if they called it a small evil, they should not have fabricated words and exalted empty prose to this extent—this differs from what one hears in the old histories.

zh: 推此而言，其稱卞、甄諸后言行之善，皆難以實論。
literal: Extending this to speak, their praise of the good conduct and words of Empresses Bian, Zhen, and the rest—all are hard to judge by reality.
idiomatic: Extending this to speak, their praise of the good conduct and words of Empresses Bian, Zhen, and the rest are all hard to judge by reality.

zh: 陳氏刪落，良有以也。
literal: Chen Shou's deletions were well founded.
idiomatic: Chen Shou's deletions were well founded.

zh: 明帝即位，有司奏請追諡，使司空王朗持節奉策以太牢告祠於陵，又別立寢廟。
literal: When Ming-di succeeded to the throne, the responsible officials memorialized requesting a posthumous title; they sent Minister of Works Wang Lang, bearing the staff of office, to present the edict with the grand sacrifice and announce the rite at the tomb, and also to establish a separate private temple.
idiomatic: When Ming-di took the throne, officials memorialized for a posthumous title. They sent Minister of Works Wang Lang with the imperial staff to offer the grand sacrifice and announce the rite at the tomb, and also to set up a separate private temple.

zh: 《魏書》載三公奏曰：「蓋孝敬之道，篤乎其親，乃四海所以承化，天地所以明察，是謂生則致其養，歿則光其靈，誦述以盡其美，宣揚以顯其名者也。
literal: The Book of Wei records that the Three Dukes submitted: "Filial reverence and respect for parents lie deep in devotion to one's kin; thereby the four seas receive transformation and heaven and earth gain clear discernment. This means that while living one renders full nurture, and after death one glorifies the spirit; recitation and narration exhaust their beauty, and proclamation and display make their names manifest."
idiomatic: The Book of Wei records the Three Dukes' memorial: "Filial reverence begins in deep devotion to one's kin. Through it the four seas receive moral instruction and heaven and earth gain clear sight. While the living owe full nurture, the dead deserve that their spirits be honored; their virtues should be recounted to the full and their names proclaimed abroad."

zh: 今陛下以聖懿之德，紹承洪業，至孝烝烝，通於神明，遭罹殷憂，每勞謙讓。
literal: Now Your Majesty, with sagely and virtuous conduct, has succeeded to the great enterprise; your utmost filial piety is abundant and reaches the spirits; having suffered deep grief, you repeatedly labor in modest yielding.
idiomatic: Your Majesty, with sagely virtue, has inherited the great enterprise. Your filial devotion reaches the spirits, and in deep grief you have repeatedly insisted on modest restraint.

zh: 先帝遷神山陵，大禮既備，至於先后，未有顯諡。
literal: The late emperor was moved to the spirit mountain tomb and the great rites were complete, yet as for the former empress, no illustrious posthumous title had been granted.
idiomatic: The late emperor had been laid in the imperial tomb and the great rites were complete, yet the former empress still lacked an illustrious posthumous title.

zh: 伏惟先后恭讓著於幽微，至行顯於不言，化流邦國，德侔二南，故能膺神靈嘉祥，為大魏世妃。
literal: I respectfully consider that the former empress's modest yielding was manifest in hidden places and her utmost conduct shone in what was left unsaid; her transforming influence flowed through the realm and her virtue matched the Two Nan odes; therefore she received the spirits' auspicious blessing and became Great Wei's consort for the ages.
idiomatic: The former empress showed modest yielding in the smallest matters and supreme conduct in deeds rather than words. Her influence flowed through the realm and her virtue matched the Two Nan odes, so she received heaven's blessing and became Great Wei's consort for the ages.

zh: 雖夙年登遐，萬載之後，永播融烈，后妃之功莫得而尚也。
literal: Although she early departed this life, after ten thousand ages her radiant glory will forever be spread abroad; the achievement of empresses and consorts cannot be surpassed.
idiomatic: Though she died young, her radiant merit will shine for ages to come; no empress or consort could surpass her.

zh: 案諡法：『聖聞周達曰昭。
literal: Examining the posthumous-title canon: 'One whose sagely repute is thorough and far-reaching is called Zhao.'
idiomatic: The canon of posthumous titles says, "One whose sagely repute is thorough and far-reaching is called Zhao."

zh: 德明有功曰昭。』
literal: One whose virtue is bright and whose merit is established is called Zhao.'
idiomatic: One whose virtue is bright and whose merit is established is called Zhao."

zh: 昭者，光明之至，盛久而不昧者也。
literal: Zhao means the utmost of brightness, flourishing long without dimming.
idiomatic: Zhao means the utmost brightness, flourishing long without fading.

zh: 宜上尊諡曰文昭皇后。」
literal: It is fitting to raise the honored posthumous title Wen-Zhao Empress."
idiomatic: We should grant the posthumous title Empress Wen-Zhao."

zh: 是月，三公又奏曰：「自古週人始祖后稷，又特立廟以祀姜嫄。
literal: That month the Three Dukes again submitted: "From antiquity the Zhou people's founding ancestor Hou Ji also had a separate temple established to sacrifice to Jiang Yuan."
idiomatic: That month the Three Dukes memorialized again: "From antiquity the Zhou people's founding ancestor Hou Ji also had a separate temple set up to honor Jiang Yuan."

zh: 今文昭皇后之於萬嗣，聖德至化，豈有量哉！
literal: Now Empress Wen-Zhao's sagely virtue and utmost transforming power toward myriad heirs—how could they be measured!
idiomatic: Empress Wen-Zhao's sagely virtue and transforming power toward all posterity—how could they be measured!

zh: 夫以皇家世
literal: Now, given the imperial house's hereditary
idiomatic: Given the imperial house's hereditary

literal: (sacrifice)
idiomatic: (sacrifice)

zh: 之尊，而克讓允恭，固推盛位，神靈遷化，而無寢廟以承享
literal: honor, yet she was able to yield and remain sincerely reverent, firmly declining the exalted position; her spirit has passed on, yet there is no private temple to receive and offer
idiomatic: honor, she yet yielded and remained sincerely reverent, firmly declining the exalted position. Her spirit has passed on, yet there is no private temple to receive and offer

literal: (rites)
idiomatic: (rites)

zh: ，非所以報顯德，昭孝敬也。
literal: —this is not the way to repay and display her manifest virtue or proclaim filial reverence.
idiomatic: —this is not how to repay her manifest virtue or proclaim filial reverence.

zh: 稽之古制，宜依周禮，先妣別立寢廟。」
literal: Examining ancient institutions, it is fitting to follow the Rites of Zhou and establish a separate private temple for the founding mother."
idiomatic: By ancient precedent and the Rites of Zhou, a separate private temple should be established for the founding mother."

zh: 並奏可之。
literal: Both memorials were submitted and approved.
idiomatic: Both memorials were approved.

zh: 太和元年227年三月，以中山魏昌之安城鄉戶千，追封逸，諡曰敬侯；
literal: In the third month of the first year of Taihe (227 CE), with the thousand households of Ancheng Township in Weichang, Zhongshan, Yi was posthumously enfeoffed and given the posthumous title Marquis Jing;
idiomatic: In the third month of Taihe 1 (227 CE), Yi was posthumously enfeoffed with the thousand households of Ancheng Township in Weichang, Zhongshan, and given the posthumous title Marquis Jing;

zh: 適孫像襲爵。
literal: his eldest grandson Xiang inherited the title.
idiomatic: his eldest grandson Xiang inherited the title.

zh: 四月，初營宗廟，掘地得玉璽，方一寸九分，其文曰「天子羨思慈親」，明帝為之改容，以太牢告廟。
literal: In the fourth month, when the ancestral temple was first being built, a jade seal was dug from the ground, one inch and nine tenths square; its inscription read "The Son of Heaven admires and thinks of his gracious parent." Ming-di changed countenance at this and announced it to the temple with the grand sacrifice.
idiomatic: In the fourth month, while the ancestral temple was first being built, workers unearthed a jade seal one inch and nine tenths square inscribed "The Son of Heaven admires and thinks of his gracious parent." Ming-di changed countenance and announced it to the temple with the grand sacrifice.

zh: 又嘗夢見后，於是差次舅氏親疏高下，敘用各有差，賞賜累鉅萬；
literal: He also once dreamed of the empress; thereupon he ranked his maternal kin by closeness and distance, high and low, appointing and employing each with distinctions, and bestowed rewards totaling tens of thousands;
idiomatic: He also once dreamed of the empress. Thereupon he ranked his maternal kin by closeness and distance, appointing each according to rank and bestowing rewards totaling tens of thousands;

zh: 以像為虎賁中郎將。
literal: Xiang was made Colonel of the Palace Guard.
idiomatic: Xiang was made Colonel of the Palace Guard.

zh: 是月，后母薨，帝制緦服臨喪，百僚陪位。
literal: That month the empress's mother died; the emperor wore the coarsest mourning and attended the funeral, and the hundred officials took their places in attendance.
idiomatic: That month the empress's mother died. The emperor wore the coarsest mourning and attended the funeral, with the hundred officials in attendance.

zh: 四年十一月，以后舊陵庳下，使像兼太尉，持節詣鄴，昭告后土，十二月，改葬朝陽陵。
literal: In the eleventh month of the fourth year, because the empress's old tomb was low and small, Xiang was made Acting Grand Commandant and sent with the staff of office to Ye to announce the rite to Queen Earth; in the twelfth month she was reburied at Chaoyang Tomb.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month of year four, because the empress's old tomb was too low and small, Xiang was made Acting Grand Commandant and sent with the imperial staff to Ye to announce the rite to Queen Earth. In the twelfth month she was reburied at Chaoyang Tomb.

zh: 像還，遷散騎常侍。
literal: When Xiang returned, he was transferred to Regular Attendant.
idiomatic: When Xiang returned, he was transferred to Regular Attendant.

zh: 青龍二年春，追諡后兄儼曰安城鄉穆侯。
literal: In the spring of the second year of Qinglong, the empress's elder brother Yan was posthumously titled Marquis Mu of Ancheng Township.
idiomatic: In the spring of Qinglong 2, the empress's elder brother Yan was posthumously titled Marquis Mu of Ancheng Township.

zh: 夏，吳賊寇揚州，以像為伏波將軍，持節監諸將東征，還，復為射聲校尉。
literal: In summer Wu bandits raided Yang Province; Xiang was made General Who Calms the Waves and, bearing the staff of office, supervised the generals in the eastern campaign; on his return he again became Colonel of the Archers Who Shoot at Sound.
idiomatic: In summer Wu forces raided Yang Province. Xiang was made General Who Calms the Waves and, bearing the imperial staff, supervised the generals on the eastern campaign. On his return he again became Colonel of the Archers Who Shoot at Sound.

zh: 三年薨，追贈衛將軍，改封魏昌縣，諡曰貞侯；
literal: In the third year he died; posthumously he was granted General of the Guard, his fief was changed to Weichang County, and he was given the posthumous title Marquis Zhen;
idiomatic: In the third year he died. He was posthumously made General of the Guard, his fief was changed to Weichang County, and he received the posthumous title Marquis Zhen;

zh: 子暢嗣。
literal: his son Chang succeeded.
idiomatic: his son Chang succeeded.

zh: 又封暢弟溫、韡、艷皆為列侯。
literal: Chang's younger brothers Wen, Wei, and Yan were also all enfeoffed as full marquises.
idiomatic: Chang's younger brothers Wen, Wei, and Yan were also all enfeoffed as full marquises.

zh: 四年，改逸、儼本封皆曰魏昌侯，諡因故。
literal: In the fourth year the original fiefs of Yi and Yan were both changed to Marquis of Weichang, their posthumous titles remaining as before.
idiomatic: In the fourth year the original fiefs of Yi and Yan were both changed to Marquis of Weichang, their posthumous titles remaining unchanged.

zh: 封儼世婦劉為東鄉君，又追封逸世婦張為安喜君。
literal: Yan's daughter-in-law Liu was enfeoffed as Lady of Dongxiang, and Yi's daughter-in-law Zhang was posthumously enfeoffed as Lady of Anxi.
idiomatic: Yan's daughter-in-law Liu was enfeoffed as Lady of Dongxiang, and Yi's daughter-in-law Zhang was posthumously enfeoffed as Lady of Anxi.
